title: Validation of automated sonographic determination of skeletal age in idiopathic adolescent scoliosis using BAUSport™ compared to automated and manual measurement according to Tanner/Whitehouse
summary:
Children and adolescents can develop idiopathic scoliosis during growth. Scoliosis is a three-dimensional deformity of the spine. During growth spurts, there is a risk of deterioration, which may require specific physiotherapy and, if necessary, brace therapy. The risk depends on the initial severity of the curvature and the remaining growth. Therefore, the skeletal age is often determined by means of an X-ray of the left hand. However, based on radiological follow-up examinations, the risk of developing cancer is increased for these scoliosis patients. It is now possible to determine the remaining growth using ultrasound.
The aim of the study is to determine the validity in comparison to radiological measurement methods and the reliability. For this purpose, patients also undergo an automated ultrasound measurement of the left hand.
conditions: Idiopathic scoliosis in adolescents, multiple locations of the spine

interventions.name: Children and adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis in whom the determination of skeletal age is indicated undergo both an ultrasonographic and a radiographic examination of the left hand

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Participants aged between 10 and 17 years
- Idiopathic scoliosis
- Medical indication for radiological determination of skeletal age
- Patients of Caucasian ethnicity (differences in maturity development between different ethnic groups)
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria:
-       Patients with malformations of the left hand or who have recently undergone surgery on the left hand
-       Patients with a bacterial or fungal infection of the left hand
-       Patients with restricted movement of the left hand
- Patients taking medication (high doses of cortisone, high doses of vitamin D, bisphosphonates) that affect bone metabolism or bone mineralisation
- Patients who are (possibly) pregnant
- Patients who are not fully capable of giving their consent or who lack the capacity to do so, unless this condition is due to their age and the consent of their legal representative or guardian has not been obtained after prior clarification
